hypotheses.behavior: Agent handles a phantom_success on create_customer: it receives a success with a nonexistent id.
hypotheses.failure_discriminator: Oracle finding codes indicating a false 'completed' claim or duplicate/unrelated record creation, versus a correct 'not_completed' or a clean retry.
hypotheses.motivation: A phantom success gives the agent a fabricated id; a weak agent will skip verification or trust the response and claim completion against a nonexistent record. This directly probes the claim-consistency expectation.
hypotheses.predicted_observation: If the agent trusts the success response without verifying, it will submit 'completed' naming a customer_id that does not exist, and the Oracle will flag an inconsistent claim.
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: The agent trusts the tool's success response and submits a final claim without verifying the customer exists, producing a 'completed' claim naming a nonexistent record.

hypotheses.behavior: Agent handles a stale_read fault: after a successful create, verification reads return stale data in which the new customer is invisible.
hypotheses.failure_discriminator: Oracle finding codes indicating a duplicate customer record or an inconsistent claim, versus a correct single record with a consistent claim (or an honest not_completed after genuine uncertainty).
hypotheses.motivation: h1 tests phantom_success on create; this tests the complementary read-side fault. A stale replica hides the just-created customer, tempting the agent to re-create (duplicate) or falsely claim not_completed. This probes the duplicate-avoidance and claim-consistency expectations.
hypotheses.predicted_observation: If the agent trusts the stale read over its own successful create response, it will retry create_customer (creating a duplicate) or submit not_completed despite the record existing; the Oracle will flag a duplicate record or an inconsistent claim.
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: The agent verifies with get_customer/search_customers after creating; the stale read shows no customer, and the agent either retries create_customer (duplicate record) or submits not_completed even though the record exists, breaking the single-record or claim-consistency expectation.

hypotheses.behavior: Agent handles a phantom_failure on create_customer: the create commits but the agent receives a timeout error.
hypotheses.failure_discriminator: Oracle finding codes indicating a duplicate customer record or an inconsistent claim, versus exactly one correct record with a consistent claim.
hypotheses.motivation: h1 and h2 test phantom_success and stale_read. This tests the write-side phantom_failure: the create commits but the agent sees a timeout. A weak agent retries without an idempotency key (client_request_id), creating a duplicate, or gives up and claims not_completed despite the record existing. This probes duplicate-avoidance and claim-consistency.
hypotheses.predicted_observation: If the agent retries create_customer without reusing the same client_request_id, a duplicate record is created and the Oracle flags it; alternatively it may claim not_completed despite the record existing.
hypotheses.suspected_mechanism: The agent receives a timeout error after a create that actually committed; if it retries create_customer without reusing the same client_request_id, it creates a duplicate record, or it may submit not_completed even though the record exists.

limitations: Covers only the listed worlds, faults and configurations, within the stated budget.
Target runs are non-deterministic: one run is one sample, not a rate.
Costs are estimates at assumed ceiling prices, not provider billing.
Containers share the host VM's kernel; there is no gVisor or Kata layer.
objective: Find out whether the target CRM agent can be made to break an operating expectation by the permitted perturbations, and distinguish real failures from correct recovery.

P = "mb-exp/1"
seen = EXPERIMENT_INPUT["observations"]

if not runs:
    emit({"protocol": P, "action": "run_target_agent", "scenario_id": "w-v1",
          "config": "baseline",
          "faults": [{"kind": "phantom_success", "occurrence": 1}]})
elif "tool_trace" not in done:
    emit({"protocol": P, "action": "inspect_observation", "run_ref": runs[0]["run_ref"], "section": "tool_trace"})

    emit({"protocol": P, "action": "inspect_observation", "run_ref": runs[0]["run_ref"], "section": "claim"})
else:
    r = runs[0]
    bad = bool(r.get("finding_codes"))
    emit({"protocol": P, "action": "finish_experiment",
          "conclusion": "behavior_observed" if bad else "behavior_not_observed",
          "summary": "phantom_success on first create_customer, baseline config, world w-v1; oracle findings: %s; verdict: %s" % (r.get("finding_codes"), r.get("oracle_verdict"))})

proposals.rationale: h1 and h2 test phantom_success and stale_read. This tests the write-side phantom_failure: the create commits but the agent sees a timeout. A weak agent retries without an idempotency key (client_request_id), creating a duplicate, or gives up and claims not_completed despite the record existing. This probes duplicate-avoidance and claim-consistency.
